title: Match the multiple to the business
intro: Three case studies where the obvious number misleads — and the lens that reads each one honestly.

steps.title: The 400× that isn't (only) a joke
steps.body:
Healthcare Global, India's largest cancer-hospital chain, screens at **~400× earnings** — an easy no. But a decade of **~₹1,700 crore in capex** (beds, LINACs, new cities, the Milann acquisition) loads depreciation onto the P&L, crushing EPS years before the capacity earns. **EV/EBITDA tells a different story.**

The honest caveat the article keeps: five-year median **ROCE is 12%** — the capital deployed hasn't earned its keep *yet*. Both lenses matter.

steps.title: The bank at 0.9× book
steps.body:
Bank of Baroda trades at **0.9× book value** — a discount to state-run peers — 'like a batsman whose poor form has a long afterlife.' The remembered sins are real (a painful exposure cleanup over a decade), but the current form is respectable: **RoA above 1%**, **RoE in the mid-teens** (FY26).

Banks are valued on **book + returns on it** — and the afterlife of poor form is where that lens finds its bargains.

steps.title: Demand that queues
steps.body:
The heat-exchanger coil maker behind the Daikin and Blue Star showrooms: its new plant 'does not need to find its market — much of it was already queuing' (customers had approved samples awaiting supply). Capacity with **pre-sold demand** is a different risk class from capacity chasing a forecast.

And the NSE IPO (₹30,000 crore, a decade after the 2016 filing froze in scandal) shows a fourth lens: sometimes the valuation question is **governance history**, not multiples.

steps.title: The rule
steps.body:
> [!key] Every multiple is a shortcut over assumptions. **P/E** breaks on depreciation-heavy expansion and turnarounds; **EV/EBITDA** sees through depreciation but forgives capital burning — pair it with **ROCE**; **P/B + RoE/RoA** is the banking lens.

The screen raises the question. The case study answers it.

recap:
**Pick the lens that matches the business model.**

- Capex-heavy: EV/EBITDA + ROCE together (HCG: better than 400× suggests, worse than EBITDA alone flatters).
- Banks: price-to-book + returns; bargains hide in form's afterlife.
- Pre-sold capacity ≠ speculative capacity.
- Optically absurd multiple → find the accounting cause first.
